newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen court orders flogging of two journalists.
newsitem.headline: Yemen court orders flogging of two journalists.

text.p: A court in Yemen on Tuesday sentenced two Yemeni journalists to 80 lashes each after finding them guilty of defaming a leading Islamist politician, one of the reporters said.
Abdullah Saad Mohammad, chief editor of the weekly al-Shura, said he and his brother Abdul-Jabar Saad, also a writer, were also banned from practicing their professions for a year.
It was the first time in recent memory that a Yemeni court sentenced a journalist to flogging, legal sources said. The sentence is usually carried out in Yemen with a thin wooden stick.
Mohammad said he and his brother would appeal against the court ruling.
Abdul-Majeed al-Zandani, a leader of the Islah political party, an influential Islamist group, filed a suit against the journalists over a year ago for critical articles that allegedly defamed him.
"The flogging (sentence) is a clear and dangerous message that threatens the freedom of the press and of expression...," Abdul-Bari Taher, head of Yemen's press association, told Reuters.
The court also ordered al-Shura to halt publication for six months and fined it 200,000 rials ($1,600), Mohammad said.
